headline: High-risk shared-workflow pair: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution and broad egress create dangerous default paths for leakage, conflict, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between emqx and Langflow, so prompt injection is not provably present. However, Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain agents, while emqx exposes HTTP APIs and broad egress; if emqx outputs are routed into a flow, Langflow may treat content as trusted. The pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF emqx outputs are copied into a Langflow flow node or uploaded file
IF Langflow components parse that content as instructions or tool arguments
mitigations: Disable any flow that forwards raw emqx output into prompt-bearing nodes
Add a provenance tag or delimiter before Langflow ingestion
Restrict uploaded files to a dedicated staging folder
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: emqx touches IoT data and has broad network egress; Langflow reads and writes server filesystem data and stores per-flow credentials. A shared workspace or uploaded-file path would let sensitive IoT data move into Langflow’s inference/backend paths. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, but the exact shared storage is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files
IF Langflow flows send file contents to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services
mitigations: Keep emqx outputs out of Langflow file uploads
Store secrets in separate vaults per agent
Rotate any credentials already loaded into Langflow
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate hosts or containers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: emqx has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while Langflow can execute shell, install packages, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Even without a documented shared directory, overlapping write and network authority can conflict if both operate on the same resources. Uncertainty remains about the exact shared target, so severity is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or service endpoint
IF Langflow flows invoke shell or package-install steps against resources emqx also updates
mitigations: Assign separate directories and service accounts
Disable shell/package steps in shared flows
Use file locks or queue-based serialization
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents and run unsandboxed Python by default, so it may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. If emqx-generated data or summaries feed into Langflow actions, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or external HTTP requests. Because the pair can create default dangerous automation, high is warranted.
conditions: IF emqx output is used as an input node in a Langflow graph
IF Langflow downstream nodes trigger HTTP calls or agent actions without verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action nodes
Require schema validation on emqx-derived inputs
Disable autonomous action nodes in shared flows
requires-engineering: add verification gates between graph stages

E_compliance.rationale: emqx touches IoT data, while Langflow stores flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials on the server filesystem. If regulated IoT data or associated identifiers are routed through Langflow, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific residency regime, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is processed in Langflow flows
IF Langflow retention or logging exceeds the policy applied to emqx data
mitigations: Minimize regulated fields before flow ingestion
Set short retention on Langflow logs and artifacts
Separate compliance-bound data from general workflows
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared retention policy
